considered.name: True Cushion Survival Horizon

considered.name: Revenue Earned Per Dollar Of Burden

This replaces the stale-minimum construction with a turnover concept rather than a cover or profitability concept — the archive has tested what a firm owns, what it earns and how it finances itself, but never how much business it transacts per unit of total economic burden. considered.name: Claims Against Peak True Capital

considered.name: Knowledge Cover Against Revenue Instability

considered.name: Working Capital Against Knowledge Burden

considered.name: Knowledge Share Of Recent Commitments

considered.name: Research Retrenchment Per Claim Dollar

critic_notes.rationale: An additive SUMRANK cannot "isolate the subset whose distress is an accounting artifact" as the hypothesis claims (a high score is achievable from either leg alone), and the second leg's expected direction — low retained-earnings/assets earning *higher* returns — contradicts the well-documented distress/RE-to-assets evidence, so the construct is both internally inconsistent and largely a repackaging of the known R&D-intensity premium.

The expression algebraically decomposes into (liabilities/assets) minus (5-year R&D stock/assets), i.e. a simple linear difference of two already-studied characteristics rather than an interaction, and netting an unrecorded *asset* against liabilities is the wrong balance-sheet adjustment (it should enter the denominator, as proposal 4 correctly does).

The hypothesis is about *debt-service* capacity but the expression subtracts the entire debt *stock* from a one-year cash flow, a stock/flow mismatch in which the debt term dominates numerically, so the signal collapses into a conventional leverage-plus-cash-flow composite with the R&D add-back contributing a third-order tilt.

This is the one genuinely interaction-by-construction proposal here — it is identically zero for non-R&D firms and largest where high book leverage coexists with a large off-balance-sheet knowledge stock — with a coherent mispricing story and outlier-robust rank differencing, though the tester should verify it is not simply a monotone proxy for R&D-to-assets by controlling for that ratio.

The unpledgeable-collateral conditioning of the known debt-issuance anomaly is an economically defensible refinement, but two construction flaws need fixing: COALESCE(xrd,0) leaves all non-R&D firms tied at a common non-zero rank rather than "switched off," and GROWTH of a leverage ratio explodes for firms with near-zero base debt.

A sensible and internally consistent operationalization of R&D-adjusted profitability that concentrates on firms near the zero-earnings threshold, but it sits close to the published R&D-capitalization/adjusted-earnings literature and duplicates the rank-wedge machinery of the leverage proposal, so it should be judged on whether it adds incremental power beyond xrd/at and pi/at separately.

The construction is internally consistent and does fix the dead short leg of the parent wedge, but because non-R&D firms are pinned near zero the signal is close to gross profitability (a well-known Novy-Marx anomaly) restricted to R&D firms, so any alpha must be shown to survive controlling for GP itself.

Sign, scaling (non-negative rank weight times signed industry-demeaned net leverage) and hypothesis all line up, and industry-demeaning plus collateral-scarcity weighting is a defensible, non-trivial refinement over the gen-0 level-based collateral ratio, though xrd/sale is fragile for near-zero-sales firms and the industry-relative leverage effect is partly documented.

Mechanically broken long leg: for the majority of firms with xrd always zero, current-minus-five-year-max is exactly 0, which is above the cross-sectional mean and therefore a positive z-score, so the long portfolio fills with high-leverage non-R&D firms rather than the "credible pseudo-distressed innovators" the hypothesis describes.

This is the third rank-wedge in the same family and, like its siblings, the rank difference is near-monotone in R&D-stock-to-assets, so it largely re-expresses the already-tested R&D intensity tilt rather than isolating a distinct accumulated-equity-depletion channel; the authors' own framing concedes it is a near-sibling diagnostic.

critic_notes.target_name: Internal Knowledge Versus Acquired Goodwill Under Debt
critic_notes.rationale: The internal-versus-acquired intangible composition angle is genuinely new relative to the archive, the expression is signed and centered consistently with the stated hypothesis, and the leverage-rank weighting is a real conditioning device — though the composition term is essentially a difference of two separately documented effects (R&D intensity positive, goodwill negative), so an incremental test against those components is warranted.

critic_notes.target_name: Working Capital Coverage Of Research Commitment
critic_notes.rationale: Because xrd is an order of magnitude smaller than lct for nearly all firms, the expression collapses to (act−lct)/lct, i.e. the current ratio minus one — a classic liquidity/solvency screen — so the claimed R&D "interaction" is economically negligible and the signal is effectively a rediscovery of a standard ratio.

This is a single-input swap (ib→oancf) on the archive's best existing signal and is largely mechanical rather than substantive, since R&D outlay is already embedded as an outflow inside oancf and the MAX(·,0) floor means that for the majority of cash-positive firms the expression collapses to plain 5-year R&D intensity — a well-known anomaly — so the "mechanism diagnostic" framing is weaker than claimed.

The post-add-back MAX is a genuine nonlinearity rather than a relabeling of the archive's difference signal, the expected negative sign follows naturally from the expression, and it cleanly isolates residual (non-R&D-explained) equity destruction — though it will be heavily correlated with the standard cumulative-loss/distress anomaly and should be judged incremental to that.

Adding COALESCE(xad,0) to the archive's best signal is a cosmetic one-term variant whose economic content barely moves, because xad is reported by a small minority of Compustat firms and is small relative to xrd where both exist, so any change in results will be driven by a thin sliver of consumer-facing names rather than by the stated brand-capital mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent (non-negative rank weight times signed, centered inverse-volatility, so non-R&D firms sit near neutral) and second-moment fragility is a genuinely untested leg in this archive, but the signal is close to a mechanical product of two separately documented effects (R&D intensity and earnings-volatility), so incremental power over each leg alone must be demonstrated.

critic_notes.target_name: Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar
critic_notes.rationale: Recasting the goodwill-composition idea as a continuous ratio is a legitimate response to the rank×z-score form's weak FMB slope, but scaling by lt makes the signal substantially a low-leverage/high-R&D composite with an unstable denominator for cash-rich, debt-light firms, so the result may reflect the leverage denominator more than the internal-versus-acquired-intangible distinction it claims to isolate.

It is a coherent, fully covered continuous benchmark for the wedge family with a sign that matches the expression's natural direction, but it double-counts realized losses (cumulative deficits already depress at and thus inflate lt/at) and is close enough to book leverage plus the accumulated-deficit distress anomaly that it needs to be evaluated against plain lt/at to show the intangible correction adds anything.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Solvency Net Of Burn Per Claim
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally coherent and monotone in the intended direction (burn hurts through both numerator and denominator), but it is fundamentally a hybrid recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new economic content, so the marginal information is limited and largely diagnostic.

This is a pure mechanical industry-demeaning of an already-evaluated archive signal with no change in economic content — a useful robustness check but not a distinct signal proposal, and the archive already contains an IND_ZSCORE variant of the leverage family.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Capitalized Five Year Earnings Record
critic_notes.rationale: TS_SUM(ib+xrd)/at is a near-linear combination of two long-published anomalies (cumulative profitability/earnings-to-assets and R&D-to-assets), and it is also a level-form restatement of the archive's "Expensing Induced Loss Illusion," so any positive result is uninterpretable as novel cross-theme evidence.

A one-year DELTA of a ratio whose numerator is a five-year sum reduces mostly to R&D-growth minus loss-change plus a large negative loading on asset growth, so the signal is confounded with two documented anomalies (R&D growth, asset growth) rather than isolating the claimed "revision in true solvency."

This is the only proposal that introduces genuinely new economic content (research output rather than input), but the positive expected sign sits uneasily with the well-documented negative sales-growth/investment premium and the mixed R&D-plus-liabilities denominator can become very small for cash-rich debt-free firms, so the interpretation will hinge on whether the scaling truly flips the sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Tax Verified Return On Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Internally inconsistent — txt is accrual-basis total tax expense, not cash taxes paid, so it does not deliver the "hard-to-fake" verification the hypothesis rests on, and cumulative tax expense over a capital base is in practice a rescaled profitability measure, i.e. a rediscovery of the profitability premium.

critic_notes.target_name: Ranked Internal Knowledge Cover Per Claim
critic_notes.rationale: This is a strictly monotone re-transform of the already-evaluated "Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar" (identical quantile sorts, by the proposer's own admission), so it is a cosmetic variant that can only move the FMB slope and adds no new economic content.

critic_notes.target_name: Liquid And Knowledge Buffer Per Claim
critic_notes.rationale: Adding cash to the non-goodwill resource base is a coherent and internally consistent economic modification of the cover-ratio family rather than a transform, though the added leg overlaps materially with the well-documented cash-holdings/liquidity return premium and the increment over the parent signal is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Share Of Total Economic Burden
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is monotone in R&D-stock/(liabilities + cumulative burn), i.e. a bounded rescaling of the knowledge-cover ratios already tested in the archive, so the "composition" framing is a distributional reparameterization rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Pre Research Cash Flow Cover Of Claims
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis (R&D as discretionary rather than committed) genuinely reverses the archive's post-research convention and the expression matches it, but the base term oancf/lt is essentially Ohlson's funds-from-operations-to-total-liabilities distress component, so much of any result will be a rediscovery of known distress/profitability pricing with an R&D add-back wrinkle.

critic_notes.target_name: Durable Research Floor Versus Rollover Need
critic_notes.rationale: With COALESCE(xrd,0) the five-year minimum is zero for the large majority of firm-years and is an order of magnitude smaller than dlc even for research firms, so the signal collapses to negative short-term-debt-to-assets — a known leverage/distress measure — and the claimed full coverage is a symptom of that degeneracy rather than a virtue.

critic_notes.target_name: Ranked Burn Adjusted Real Intangible Cover
critic_notes.rationale: Denominator and most of the numerator are identical to the already-evaluated "Knowledge Solvency Net Of Burn Per Claim," so once the rank transform is recognized as monotone the only genuine change is subtracting goodwill, making this an incremental variant dressed up as a consolidation test.

critic_notes.target_name: Funds From Operations Before Research Per Claim
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Pre Research Cash Flow Cover Of Claims" with a missing-data fallback bolted on, i.e., a coverage patch rather than a new economic mechanism — and substituting `ib` for `oancf` silently changes the construct being measured (net income vs. operating cash flow) in exactly the pre-1987 subsample the test is supposed to validate, so a "survives" result is uninterpretable.

critic_notes.target_name: Stock And Flow Knowledge Solvency Screen
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis is explicitly conjunctive ("passes both tests"), but SUMRANK is additive and lets a top score on one leg fully compensate for a bottom score on the other — the stated economics would require a MIN/double-sort construction — and as written it is an ensemble average of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new content.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Solvency Against Risk Weighted Claims
critic_notes.rationale: Adding a dollar earnings-volatility term to the claim base is a genuinely new second-moment dimension in an archive of purely first-moment denominators and is economically motivated, though it remains a denominator refinement of an existing high-scoring signal and inherits that family's non-monotonicity when the numerator is negative (a larger denominator then *raises* the score), which should be checked before over-reading the slope.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Build Up Instead Of Research
critic_notes.rationale: This is a fixed-weight linear combination of two well-known published anomalies (Sloan accruals and R&D intensity), both of which already carry the expected negative sign, so a strong result is a rediscovery rather than an interaction — and worse, the `COALESCE(oancf, ib)` fallback makes the accrual term identically zero pre-1987, collapsing the signal to pure negative R&D intensity over a third of the sample.

critic_notes.target_name: Three Year Research Versus Debt Build
critic_notes.rationale: A pure lookback-window change (5→3 years) on an already-evaluated archive signal is the definition of a cosmetic variant; the coverage gain is real but does not constitute a distinct economic hypothesis and should not consume a generation slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquired Intangible Share Of True Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The knowledge-stock term in the denominator is a second-order adjustment, so the signal is essentially goodwill-to-assets — a documented acquisition/intangible-composition anomaly — and with `COALESCE(gdwl, 0)` the majority of firms pile up at exactly zero, making the short leg a near-binary "has goodwill" screen rather than a cross-theme composition measure.

A three-year cumulation of the archive's already-tested one-year equity-issuance-net-of-R&D signal is essentially a lookback extension, and the three-year change in book equity net of retained earnings is very close to the published composite/net equity issuance anomaly, so the R&D subtraction is doing too little work to make this a distinct test.

Equity issuance plus net debt issuance scaled by assets is the well-documented net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), and since the archive already has both legs separately their sum with an R&D offset is more likely a rediscovery plus arithmetic than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Weakest Link Of Cover And Self Funding
critic_notes.rationale: The conjunction is internally consistent (the NEG correctly orients the financing leg so that high values mean self-funded and the positive sign follows), and joining a stock-cover test to a near-orthogonal flow-financing test via a no-compensation MIN is a substantive economic claim rather than a cosmetic blend, though it does inherit correlation with both parent signals.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Cover Of Claims And Burn
critic_notes.rationale: The non-monotonicity diagnosis is legitimate and well-reasoned, but the resulting expression sits directly between two already-tested archive ratios (knowledge stock per liability dollar and knowledge-net-of-burn per claim), differing only by moving the burn term across the fraction bar, so it is likely to be highly collinear with existing results rather than decisive.

Excluding purchased intangibles while adding the unrecorded research stock is a coherent and genuinely new-to-the-archive pair of adjustments, but the resulting quantity is a tangible-plus-knowledge net worth ratio that overlaps materially with the existing knowledge-stock-net-of-debt and pledgeable-collateral signals, capping its expected incremental information.

critic_notes.target_name: Pre Research Earnings Over Risk Weighted Claims
critic_notes.rationale: This simply crosses an already-tested numerator (pre-research earnings over liabilities, embedded in the gen-5 MIN screen) with an already-tested denominator (risk-weighted claims), and any gain from the at·VOL(ib/at) term is hard to distinguish from the known earnings-volatility/low-volatility anomaly rather than the proposed liquidity-buffer channel.

The loss-year conditioning is a genuine tightening of the archive's best cross-sectional idea rather than a cosmetic re-scaling, but it creates a large mass point at exactly zero for consistently profitable firms, which collapses cross-sectional dispersion in the middle and makes the resulting spread essentially a within-loss-maker sort — worth testing, but the degenerate ranking should be diagnosed if results weaken.

critic_notes.target_name: Risk Weighted Cover With Self Funding
critic_notes.rationale: This is a single-leg substitution inside an already-validated MIN structure whose two candidate cover legs (goodwill-netted knowledge cover and burn-adjusted risk-weighted cover) are constructed from largely the same numerator and both scale by liabilities, so it is a cosmetic variant of the champion rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Stacking a third nested MIN on an already-tested two-way conjunction is incremental leg-permutation rather than a new economic mechanism, and because MIN of three ranks drives the extremes toward whichever leg is sparsest it predictably thins and destabilizes the tails — exactly the coverage/composition artifact the objective warns against.

R&D-added-back earnings over an intangible-augmented capital base is a direct rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted profitability/ROIC anomaly (and overlaps the archive's "Expensing Induced Loss Illusion"), and since profitability is an explicit FF5 factor the abnormal-alpha content is likely to be largely spanned.

The MAX "fails either test" structure is a coherent and correctly signed short-side counterpart to the validated MIN logic and combines two near-orthogonal fragility channels, though the issuance leg is close to the well-known net-equity-issuance anomaly, so the incremental content rests mainly on the goodwill-overhang term.

Substituting a full-coverage worst-year realization test for the financing leg is a legitimate ablation that isolates whether financing dependence is specifically necessary or whether any orthogonal second screen delivers the Sharpe gain, but it remains one more permutation of an already heavily explored conjunction family and should be the only such variant carried forward.

This is essentially the arithmetic difference of two already-evaluated archive signals (the MIN conjunction with fmb 4.92 and the MAX disjunction with fmb −5.29), so a strong result is close to mechanically guaranteed by construction and teaches nothing new about the economics — it is a portfolio blend dressed as a hypothesis, and it re-uses the goodwill/knowledge-stock terms on both sides, partially cancelling them.

Wrapping the archive's existing cover ratio (xrd5 − gdwl)/lt in TS_MIN is a one-operator cosmetic variant, and because the numerator is itself a five-year cumulative sum of a highly persistent quantity, the five-year minimum is close to a mechanically stale, four-year-lagged version of the parent rather than a genuine "durability" measure.

A pure denominator swap (lt → dltt+dlc) on an existing archive ratio, and the swap introduces a construction problem the reasoning ignores: firms with near-zero financial debt produce explosive or undefined ratios whose cross-sectional ordering is essentially arbitrary, so any apparent gain would be a low-debt-firm artifact rather than evidence about claim definition.

With xrd coalesced to zero the signal collapses exactly to three-year liability growth scaled by assets for the large non-R&D majority, making it a direct rediscovery of the well-documented asset/liability-growth and net-operating-liabilities anomalies, and the R&D term is too small relative to Δlt to change the ranking for most firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst Year Post Research Margin Cover
critic_notes.rationale: It is a crossing of two archive parents rather than a new mechanism, but the diagnostic question it poses — whether the worst-year effect comes from operating capacity or from write-down noise in the bottom line — is well-posed, the expression matches the hypothesis, and coverage should be full.

critic_notes.target_name: Fails Either Non Issuance Fragility Test
critic_notes.rationale: The stated robustness motivation is legitimate, but the replacement leg is the same liability-growth construct flagged above as a likely rediscovery of the asset-growth anomaly, so this would substitute one known published effect (net equity issuance) for another rather than establishing that the disjunction survives on genuinely cross-theme information.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Share Of Risk Bearing Capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially a denominator swap on the archive's already-strongest ratio ((xrd5−gdwl)/lt, alpha 6.4%, t 4.76), and the stated boundedness claim is only half true — the ratio is capped above at 1 but is unbounded below for goodwill-heavy firms, so the "cannot explode" motivation does not hold as written.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Mix And Worst Year Conjunction
critic_notes.rationale: This is the fifth leg-substitution in the same MIN-conjunction family (financing, product-market, cover-level partners already tested) and it retains the champion's worst-year leg verbatim while swapping in a knowledge/debt share that duplicates proposal #1, so it is a permutation rather than a new mechanism.

Both numerator and denominator differ substantively from the earnings-volatility-weighted predecessor, and product-market/demand instability as the stress weight on the claim base is an economically distinct channel that the archive has never used, with a natural positive sign and full coverage.

This is a mechanical MAX of two already-evaluated archive signals and merely swaps the goodwill leg out of the existing "Fails Either Fragility Test," so the cross-sectional slope will be inherited almost entirely from the issuance leg (fmb −5.20) rather than reflecting any new economics.

Total liabilities are highly persistent, so TS_MAX(lt,5) ≈ lt for the large majority of firms and this is a near-collinear cosmetic rescaling of the archive's existing "Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar" with the identical numerator.

Another leg swap in the saturated MIN-conjunction family whose new leg (cash/current liabilities) is a plain, well-documented liquidity/cash-holdings measure, and the proposal itself concedes it is a robustness check rather than a new mechanism.
